summary: WebAssembly is a compact, safe and portable binary code format with a precisely defined instruction set and execution rules; it is a target that many programming languages compile to, not a format for scenes, avatars or media. It covers the safe running of untrusted code well: modules are validated before use, run isolated from their host, and can reach the outside world only through functions the host chooses to supply. It also has a strong change story: a backward-compatibility promise, a version field, ignorable custom sections for extensions, named language subsets including a deterministic one, and a public conformance test suite. It leaves everything about worlds to others: scenes, avatars, networking, identity, sensing, rendering, and even input and output, because the core specification defines no way to talk to any environment and leaves that to separate interface documents for each hosting environment. Trap for a standards audience: two hosts can run the same module only if both supply the same imports, so the claim that a platform runs WebAssembly says nothing about whether guest content written for another platform will work there. The address ending in wasm-core-2 now serves release 3.0 of the core specification, not release 2.0.

coverage.note: The core specification requires validation before execution and gives a module no ambient access to its host; the host decides which functions a module may import.
